questions.question: 'Memoirs of Babur' or 'Baburnama', also known as 'Tuzk-e Babri', was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Babur.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Babur has written his biography i.e. Baburnama which is also known as Tuzk-e Babri. Babur and Jahangir are the only two emperors of the Mughal Empire who wrote their own biographies.**
 
• Baburnama is also known to be the first true autobiography in Islamic literature.
 
• Baburnama was written in **Chagatai Turkic**, which was Babur's mother tongue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuzk-e Babri** is written in the Chagatai language, known to Babur as Turki (meaning Turkic), the spoken language of the Timurids.
 
• As the Mughals were Chaghtai Turks by origin, Turkish was their mother tongue.
 
• Tuzk-e Babri is the memoirs of **Zahir-ud-Dīn Muhammad Bābur (1483- 1530),** founder of the Mughal Empire and a great-great-great-grandson of Timur.
 
• During Emperor Akbar's reign, the work was completely translated to Persian, the usual literary language of the Mughal court by a Mughal

 courtier, Abdul Rahim.
 
• It was Akbar who consciously set out to make Persian the leading language of the Mughal court.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the winners of Nobel Prize in Physics 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **Roger Penrose.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Roger Penrose** was one of the winners of the Nobel Prize in Physics 2020.
 
• Roger Penrose of** Britain, Reinhard Genzel of Germany, and Andrea Ghez of the US won the Nobel Physics Prize for 2020.**
 
• The physicists were selected for their discoveries about one of the most exotic phenomena in the universe, the black hole.
 
• Andrea Ghez is just the fourth woman to receive the physics prize since** 1901 when the first Nobel prizes** were handed out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Roger Penrose** used ingenious mathematical methods in his proof that black holes are a direct consequence of Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity.
 
• Einstein did not himself believe that black holes really exist, these super-heavyweight monsters that capture everything that enters them. Nothing can escape, not even light.
 
• **Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez **each lead a group of astronomers that, since the early 1990s, have focused on a region called **Sagittarius A*** at the centre of our galaxy.
 
• Their pioneering work has given us the most convincing evidence yet of a supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Loktak Lake located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Manipur.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India and is famous for the phumdis a series of floating islands) floating over it.**
 
• The lake is located near Moirang town in** Manipur state.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Phumdis are heterogeneous masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter at various stages of decomposition.
 
• Phumdis play an important role in the ecological processes and functions of the lake ecosystem.
 
• The largest single mass of phumdi is in the southeastern part of the lake, covering an area of 40 km2.
 
• This mass constitutes the world's largest floating park, named Keibul Lamjao National Park.
 
 
• It serves as a source of water for irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydropower generation.
 
• Status: Ramsar Wetland: 1990.
 
• Listed in Montreux Record in 1993.

questions.question: Who among the following was the President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) as of December 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sourav Ganguly.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sourav Chandidas Ganguly, affectionately known as Dada, is the 39th and the current president of the Board of Control for Cricket in India, an Indian cricket administrator, commentator, and former national cricket team captain.**
 
• On October 23, 2019, Ganguly became the 39th BCCI president, thus ending the** 33-month reign of the Supreme Court-appointed Committee of ****Administrators (CoA)** to run the cricket board's daily affairs.
 
• Sourav Ganguly is only the second cricketer from India to become the president of the BCCI.
 
• Ganguly, who played **113 tests and 311 one-day internationals and led ****India to 21 test wins**, has already been an administrator for the Cricket Association of Bengal, his home state association (CAB).
 
• In the past, he was part of the BCCI's technical panel and also, alongside** ****Sachin Tendulkar and VVS Laxman, part of a three-member Cricket Advisory Committee.​**

questions.question: Since 2000, Euro norms are followed in India under the name _____ Stage Emission Standards for four wheeled vehicles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bharat.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Since 2000, Euro norms are followed in India under the name** Bharat Stage Emission Standards for four-wheeled vehicles.**
 
• In 13 major cities,** Bharat Stage IV emission** norms have been in place since April 2010 and it has been enforced for the entire country since April 2017.
 
• **In 2016, **the Indian government announced that the country would skip the** BS V norms altogether and adopt BS-VI norms by 2020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vehicle emission norms were introduced in India in** 1991 for petrol and in 1992** for diesel vehicles.
 
• Since 2000, Euro norms are followed in India under the name Bharat Stage Emission Standards for four-wheeled vehicles. Bharat stage III norms have been enforced across India since October 2010.
 
• **The National Auto Fuel Policy 2003** introduced certain emission requirements for interstate buses with routes originating or terminating in Delhi or the other mentioned cities.
 
• **For 2-and 3-wheelers, Bharat Stage Il applied from April 1, 2005, and Stage III standards came into force on April 1, 2010.**

questions.question: In which of the following mountain ranges will you find the Guru Shikhar peak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Aravalli.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Shikhar Peak is located in the Arbuda Mountains of Rajasthan.**
 
• **It is the highest point of the Aravalli Range situated at 1,722 meters.**
 
• It is named** Guru-Shikhar or 'the peak of the guru' after Dattatreya, an incarnation of Vishnu, and a cave at the summit contains a temple dedicated to him, plus one dedicated to his mother, Anasuya, wife of sage Atri.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range:**

 
 
• It is a part of the **Deccan plateau. It is a series of seven mountains. Hence, called Satpura.**
 
• It runs in an east-west direction south of the Vindhyas and in between the Narmada and the Tapi, roughly parallel to these rivers.
 
• It stretches for a distance of about** 900 km.**
 
• Dhupgarh which is** 1,350 m** high is located near** Pachmarhi on Mahadev Hills.**
 
 
 
• **The Vindhya Range:**
 
 
• It is a complex, discontinuous chain of mountain ridges, hill ranges, highlands, and plateau escarpments in** West-central India.**
 
• The Vindhya range mostly extends through the Indian states of** Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• **​The Karakoram Range:**
 
 
• It is a mountain range spanning the borders of **China, India, and Pakistan, with the northwest extremity of the range extending to Afghanistan and Tajikistan.**
 
• **It is the second-highest mountain range **in the world. It is a part of the complex of ranges including the Pamir Mountains, the Hindu Kush, and the Himalayan Mountains. The Karakoram Highway connects China-Pakistan.
 
• The range has eight mountains with tops over **7,500 meters (24,600 ft) high**.
 
• **Four of these are higher than 8,000 meters (26,000 ft). They are K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, and Gasherbrum II.**

questions.question: Litmus paper changes to ______ colour when put in soap water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Blue.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Litmus paper changes to a** blue ****colour** when put in soap water.
 
• Indicators are the substances that are used to identify whether the given substance is an acid or a base.
 
• There are two types of indicators:
 
• **Natural:**
 
 
• These indicators are obtained from natural sources like plants.
 
• Turmeric, litmus, china rose petals, etc., are some of the naturally occurring indicators.
 
• The most commonly used natural indicator is litmus.
 
• It is extracted from lichens.
 
• It is available in the form of a solution, or in the form of strips of paper, known as litmus paper.
 
 
 
• **Man-made:**
 
 
• Phenolphthalein, Methyl orange are some of the man-made indicators.
